pointers.sentence: Since 5.1 the request methods of `RequestFactory`, `AsyncRequestFactory`, `Client` and `AsyncClient` take `query_params=`, a mapping made the query string (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory.generic`).

`ClientMixin.asession`, `ClientMixin.alogin`, `ClientMixin.aforce_login` and `ClientMixin.alogout` (5.0) are coroutine twins of the session and the login and logout methods (`django/test/client.py:ClientMixin.alogin`; [Sessions and logins in the test client: `ClientMixin.login` and `force_login`](../testing/client-login.md#the-asynchronous-methods)).

`AsyncClient`'s methods have taken `follow=True` since 5.0, but `ClientMixin._follow_redirect`, which it shares with `Client`, reads two keys of a WSGI environ its requests lack: under all four releases a relative `"Location"` raises `KeyError: 'PATH_INFO'`, and otherwise a 307 or 308 `KeyError: 'REQUEST_METHOD'` (`django/test/client.py:ClientMixin._follow_redirect`).

Before 6.2 that was the first entry of `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` with a get_user method, which `BaseBackend` gives every subclass, returning `None`; since 6.2 it is the first whose class overrides `BaseBackend.get_user` or `BaseBackend.aget_user`, so that "permission-only backends", the notes say, are passed over (`django/test/client.py:ClientMixin._get_backend`, `docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

Since 6.1 `SimpleTestCase._assert_contains`, which `SimpleTestCase.assertContains` and `SimpleTestCase.assertNotContains` share, sets `StreamingHttpResponse.streaming_content` again from the bytes it read (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._assert_contains`).

Since 5.1, "to enforce test isolation" (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`), it also replaces `BaseDatabaseWrapper.ensure_connection` while the class runs: under all four releases a query in a thread a test started raises `DatabaseOperationForbidden` for "threaded connections" (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.ensure_connection_patch_method`; [Which databases a test uses: `databases`](../testing/test-databases.md)).

Since 5.1, "to enforce test isolation" (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`), it also replaces `BaseDatabaseWrapper.ensure_connection` while the class runs: under all four releases a query in a thread a test started raises `DatabaseOperationForbidden` for "threaded connections" (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.ensure_connection_patch_method`; [Which databases a test uses: `databases`](../testing/test-databases.md)).

`django/test/testcases.py` sets `__unittest = True`, by which `unittest` cuts the module's frames from a failure's traceback, so a failing assertion of Django's is reported at the test's line and, the notes add, `--pdb` enters the test (`django/test/testcases.py:__unittest`).

`TransactionTestCase.setUpClass` runs `TransactionTestCase._pre_setup` for the first test, and marks `SimpleTestCase._pre_setup_ran_eagerly` so that the test does not run it again (`django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase.setUpClass`; [Emptying the tables after each test: `TransactionTestCase`](../testing/transaction-test-case.md)).

Since 6.0 it does the same under forkserver, and `get_max_test_processes`, which `--parallel auto` asks, no longer answers 1 for it (`django/test/runner.py:_init_worker`, `django/test/runner.py:get_max_test_processes`; [Running in parallel: `ParallelTestSuite`](../testing/parallel.md)).

Since 6.0 it does the same under forkserver, and `get_max_test_processes`, which `--parallel auto` asks, no longer answers 1 for it (`django/test/runner.py:_init_worker`, `django/test/runner.py:get_max_test_processes`; [Running in parallel: `ParallelTestSuite`](../testing/parallel.md)).

The argument `extra_tests=` of `DiscoverRunner.build_suite` and `DiscoverRunner.run_tests`, removed in 5.0, is taken by their `**kwargs` and ignored: under all four releases a test given in it is left out of the suite without a word (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.build_suite`).

Since 6.1 a project may name its email backends by alias in the setting `MAILERS`; `setup_test_environment` gives each alias the local-memory backend, and sets `EMAIL_BACKEND` only without `MAILERS` (`django/test/utils.py:setup_test_environment`; [What changed in mail and tasks](mail-and-tasks.md)).

A `TransactionTestCase` with `TransactionTestCase.serialized_rollback` gets back before each test the rows migrations wrote, which the runner's `setup_databases` serializes once every test database is made (`django/test/utils.py:setup_databases`; [Test databases: `BaseDatabaseCreation`](../backends/creation.md)).

Nothing warns of the new default: a project's runner that relies on it serializes nothing, and `TransactionTestCase._fixture_setup` restores no rows (`django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase._fixture_setup`).

The warning's message points to DatabaseCreation.serialize_test_db, which no class defines; the notes name `BaseDatabaseCreation.serialize_db_to_string` (`django/db/backends/base/creation.py:BaseDatabaseCreation.create_test_db`; [What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](deprecations.md)).
